name: 富兰克林·德拉诺·罗斯福

points.title: 贵族童年
points.description: 罗斯福出生于纽约州海德公园的一个富裕家庭，属于荷兰裔美国上流社会。他的父亲詹姆斯·罗斯福是一位铁路高管，母亲萨拉·德拉诺来自富有的德拉诺家族。罗斯福从小接受私人教育，由家庭教师教导，度过了无忧无虑的童年。这段经历培养了他对公共服务的早期兴趣，同时也让他熟悉了权力和特权。他的童年经历塑造了他后来对政治和社会问题的独特视角，使他既理解精英阶层的思维方式，又对普通民众的困境有所同情。
points.descriptionEn: Roosevelt was born in Hyde Park, New York, into a wealthy family of Dutch descent. His father James Roosevelt was a railroad executive, and his mother Sara Delano came from the wealthy Delano family. Roosevelt received private education from tutors and spent a carefree childhood. This experience fostered his early interest in public service while also familiarizing him with power and privilege. His childhood shaped his unique perspective on political and social issues, allowing him to understand both the mindset of the elite and the plight of ordinary citizens.

points.title: 政治崛起
points.description: 罗斯福在哈佛大学接受教育，后进入哥伦比亚大学法学院学习。1907年获得律师资格后，进入华尔街工作。1910年，他作为民主党人竞选纽约州参议员成功，开启政治生涯。1913年，他被伍德罗·威尔逊总统任命为海军助理部长，在这个职位上他展现了出色的行政管理能力。1920年，他作为民主党副总统候选人参加大选，虽然失败，但提高了全国知名度。这一时期，罗斯福建立了广泛的政治人脉，积累了丰富的政府工作经验，并形成了自己的政治理念，为后来的总统生涯奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Roosevelt attended Harvard University and later studied at Columbia Law School. After becoming a lawyer in 1907, he worked on Wall Street. In 1910, he successfully ran for the New York State Senate as a Democrat, beginning his political career. In 1913, President Woodrow Wilson appointed him Assistant Secretary of the Navy, where he demonstrated excellent administrative skills. In 1920, he ran as the Democratic vice-presidential candidate, losing but gaining national recognition. During this period, Roosevelt built extensive political connections, accumulated rich government experience, and formed his own political philosophy, laying the foundation for his later presidency.

points.title: 战胜病魔
points.description: 1921年，罗斯福在加拿大度假期间患上了脊髓灰质炎（小儿麻痹症），导致双腿永久瘫痪。这一灾难性事件本可能终结他的政治生涯，但罗斯福展现了非凡的毅力和决心。他积极寻求治疗，在佐治亚州的温泉建立了康复中心，不仅为自己寻找治疗方法，也为其他脊髓灰质炎患者提供帮助。在康复期间，罗斯福重新思考了自己的政治理念，更加关注弱势群体的困境。这段经历也使他学会了如何在公众面前隐藏自己的残疾，塑造了他坚韧不拔的形象，为他后来重新进入政坛并最终当选总统奠定了重要基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1921, while vacationing in Canada, Roosevelt contracted polio, which left his legs permanently paralyzed. This potentially career-ending event demonstrated Roosevelt's extraordinary resilience and determination. He actively sought treatment and established a rehabilitation center in Warm Springs, Georgia, not only for himself but also to help other polio patients. During his recovery, Roosevelt rethought his political philosophy and developed greater concern for the plight of vulnerable groups. This experience also taught him how to conceal his disability from the public, shaping his image of perseverance and laying an important foundation for his political comeback and eventual presidency.

points.title: 总统任期
points.description: 1933年，罗斯福在大萧条最严重时期就任美国第32任总统。他实施了著名的'新政'（New Deal），包括建立社会保障体系、实施金融改革、创造就业机会等措施，帮助美国经济复苏。面对经济危机，他通过'炉边谈话'直接与民众沟通，恢复了公众信心。1939年，第二次世界大战爆发，罗斯福领导美国逐步从孤立主义转向国际主义，通过《租借法案》支持盟国。1941年珍珠港事件后，罗斯福正式对轴心国宣战，领导美国成为'民主国家的兵工厂'。在战争期间，他与丘吉尔、斯大林等盟国领导人密切合作，共同规划战后世界秩序。罗斯福是美国历史上唯一一位连任四届的总统，他的领导对美国和世界产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1933, at the height of the Great Depression, Roosevelt was inaugurated as the 32nd President of the United States. He implemented the famous 'New Deal,' including establishing a social security system, financial reforms, and job creation programs to help the U.S. economy recover. Facing the economic crisis, he communicated directly with the public through 'Fireside Chats,' restoring public confidence. In 1939, as World War II broke out, Roosevelt led the U.S. gradually shifting from isolationism to internationalism, supporting allies through the Lend-Lease Act. After the Pearl Harbor attack in 1941, Roosevelt formally declared war on the Axis powers, leading the U.S. to become the 'arsenal of democracy.' During the war, he worked closely with Allied leaders like Churchill and Stalin to plan the post-war world order. Roosevelt was the only U.S. president to be elected to four terms, and his leadership had a profound impact on America and the world.

points.title: 逝世与遗产
points.description: 1945年4月12日，罗斯福在佐治亚州温泉度假时因突发脑溢血去世，享年63岁。他的去世震惊了世界，正值二战胜利前夕。罗斯福的遗体被运回华盛顿，随后安葬于海德公园家族墓地。作为20世纪最重要的政治领袖之一，罗斯福的遗产深远而复杂。他重塑了美国政府的角色，扩大了联邦政府的权力，建立了现代福利国家体系。在国际舞台上，他推动了联合国的成立，奠定了战后国际秩序的基础。尽管他的新政政策存在争议，且在二战期间的一些决策受到批评，但他领导美国度过大萧条和世界大战的成就使他成为美国历史上最受尊敬的总统之一，其政治理念和政策影响延续至今。
points.descriptionEn: On April 12, 1945, Roosevelt died of a cerebral hemorrhage at age 63 while vacationing in Warm Springs, Georgia. His death shocked the world, occurring just before the victory in World War II. His body was transported to Washington and later buried in the family cemetery at Hyde Park. As one of the most important political leaders of the 20th century, Roosevelt's legacy is profound and complex. He reshaped the role of the U.S. government, expanding federal power and establishing the modern welfare state system. On the international stage, he promoted the establishment of the United Nations, laying the foundation for the post-war international order. Although his New Deal policies were controversial and some of his wartime decisions were criticized, his achievements in leading America through the Great Depression and World War II make him one of the most respected presidents in U.S. history, with his political ideas and policies continuing to influence the world today.

supporter.zh: 罗斯福被视为美国历史上最伟大的总统之一，他的领导力在大萧条和世界大战期间拯救了美国。支持者赞扬他通过新政建立了现代福利国家，为普通民众提供了经济保障。他扩大了联邦政府的权力，使政府成为积极解决问题的力量。在国际舞台上，罗斯福领导美国成为反法西斯同盟的核心，推动了联合国的建立，为战后国际秩序奠定了基础。他的'唯一恐惧就是恐惧本身'的激励性话语，以及与民众直接沟通的方式，展现了非凡的政治智慧和领导才能。
supporter.en: Roosevelt is regarded as one of America's greatest presidents, whose leadership saved the nation during the Great Depression and World War II. Supporters praise him for establishing the modern welfare state through the New Deal, providing economic security for ordinary citizens. He expanded the power of the federal government, making it an active force in solving problems. On the international stage, Roosevelt led the U.S. as the core of the anti-fascist alliance and promoted the establishment of the United Nations, laying the foundation for the post-war international order. His inspirational phrase 'the only thing we have to fear is fear itself' and his direct communication with the people demonstrated extraordinary political wisdom and leadership.

critic.zh: 批评者认为罗斯福的政策存在严重问题。新政虽然缓解了经济危机，但并未真正结束大萧条，一些干预措施反而延长了经济复苏时间。他扩大联邦权力的做法被批评为威胁了美国宪法规定的三权分立和州权。在二战期间，罗斯福的决策也存在争议，如珍珠港事件前的情报忽视、日裔美国人拘留令等。此外，他试图扩大最高法院人数以推行新政的做法被视为对司法独立的威胁。批评者还指出，罗斯福的领导风格有时过于专断，缺乏足够的制衡机制。
critic.en: Critics argue that Roosevelt's policies had serious flaws. While the New Deal alleviated the economic crisis, it didn't truly end the Great Depression, and some intervention measures actually prolonged the economic recovery. His expansion of federal power is criticized as threatening the constitutional separation of powers and states' rights. During World War II, Roosevelt's decisions were also controversial, including intelligence failures before Pearl Harbor and the internment of Japanese Americans. Additionally, his attempt to expand the Supreme Court to implement the New Deal was seen as a threat to judicial independence. Critics also note that his leadership style was sometimes overly autocratic, lacking sufficient checks and balances.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，罗斯福被定义为一位转型型总统，他重新定义了美国政府的角色和公民与国家的关系。他的形象常与'新政'、'炉边谈话'和二战领导联系在一起。罗斯福的残疾成为他坚韧不拔的象征，尽管他极力在公众面前掩饰这一点。历史学家普遍认为，罗斯福的领导风格结合了实用主义和理想主义，能够灵活应对危机。他的政策既有创新也有争议，反映了20世纪美国政治的复杂性。在流行文化中，罗斯福常被描绘为危机中的领袖，他的形象超越了党派分歧，成为美国国家认同的重要象征。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Roosevelt is defined as a transformative president who redefined the role of the U.S. government and the relationship between citizens and the state. His image is often associated with the 'New Deal,' 'Fireside Chats,' and wartime leadership. Roosevelt's disability became a symbol of his resilience, though he极力 concealed it from the public. Historians generally view Roosevelt's leadership style as combining pragmatism and idealism, enabling him to flexibly respond to crises. His policies were both innovative and controversial, reflecting the complexity of 20th-century American politics. In popular culture, Roosevelt is often portrayed as a leader in times of crisis, his image transcending partisan divisions to become an important symbol of American national identity.

self.zh: 我们唯一需要恐惧的就是恐惧本身。
self.en: The only thing we have to fear is fear itself.

others.zh: 他是一位战争中的领袖，一位和平中的领袖，一位经济危机中的领袖，一位精神危机中的领袖。
others.en: He was a war leader, a peace leader, a leader in economic crisis, a leader in spiritual crisis.
